title: Does folic acid change arsenic methylation?

grade.title: Several consistent human randomized trials
grade.basis: Gamble 2006 and the FACT trial (Peters 2015, with metabolites in Bozack 2019) are consistent randomized trials. Bozack 2019 is the same trial as Peters 2015, not a third independent trial.

answerHtml: Two randomized trials found that folic acid increased the percentage of urinary arsenic excreted as dimethylarsinic acid, a methylation product. In the larger trial, 800 µg/day lowered blood arsenic and 400 µg/day did not. This is evidence about arsenic methylation, not evidence that folic acid removes stored arsenic or treats arsenicosis.

sections.heading: Trials
sections.html:
Folic acid trials with an arsenic outcome. Doses are what the trials used, not a recommendation.
StudyDesignResult
Gamble 2006 RCT, 12 weeks, 200 folate-deficient adults in Bangladesh Urinary percent DMA rose from 72 to 79 percent versus placebo (P<0.0001). PMID 17093162.
Peters 2015 FACT RCT, 24 weeks, 622 arsenic-exposed adults in Bangladesh, mostly folate sufficient 800 µg/day lowered blood arsenic. 400 µg/day did not. PMID 25978852.
Bozack 2019 Same FACT trial Folic acid increased percent DMA, with rebound after stopping. PMID 30590411. Not an independent replication.
